correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the average-roughness definition and weighted formulation, uses explicit positive \(\ell_q\) norming vectors, derives the finite lower bound by Minkowski and weighted factor inequalities, proves the universal finite upper bound by a uniform scalar expansion and Hölder inequality, and obtains the infinite case by axis tests of arbitrary finite cardinality. The error term has exponent \(\min\{p,2\}>1\), so it vanishes after division by the perturbation norm.

value.rationale: Average roughness is a quantitative form of octahedral geometry. The theorem gives the exact dependence on the number of \(\ell_p\)-summands for octahedral factors and a sharp finite-versus-infinite transition that is invisible in the binary theorem. The infinite collapse shows that arbitrarily many transverse coordinates destroy every positive average-roughness modulus even when each coordinate space is maximally average rough.
